changes: Explicit in-app microphone consent before capture, separate from OS permission; persisted locally without automatic recording.
Actual bounded analyser amplitude forwarded only from the recorder the Assistant still owns; source distinguishes a quiet attached microphone from no source.
Optional inline Avatar Studio preview stays on the Assistant page during recording; labelled source and simulated fallback, still timelines for compact reduced-motion preview.
Cancelling, revoking consent, navigating away, device loss, size/time limits release capture resources; stale asynchronous recording/decode/transcript completions cannot replace current state.
Halted capture closes its analyser, clears scheduled animation and resets amplitude; late frames cannot publish stale levels. Provider hold timer is cleared on unmount.
limitations: Tests use fake browser audio APIs and server rendering; actual microphone, Windows recognition, pointer interaction and live avatar rendering still require manual acceptance.
An already dispatched transcription request cannot be aborted through the current shared API; cancellation/revocation discards its returned transcript.
Windows TTS does not expose speech amplitude; no invented TTS lip sync or unattended microphone capture.
Avatar Studio on its separate route receives no live microphone because navigating away correctly cancels Assistant recording. The inline preview provides simultaneous source and host.
No external API calls, real microphone access, shared-contract edits, dependencies, App edits, commits or push performed by this local continuation.
